title: Counting under way in Holborn and St Pancras byelection – UK politics live
summary:
Results are expected from 2.30am BST in the north London poll to choose a replacement for former PM Keir Starmer

A quick reminder of

blocks.text: Counting under way in Holborn and St Pancras byelection
Hello and welcome to the UK politics live blog.
Counting is currently under way in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection in north London, where voters are choosing a replacement for former prime minister Sir Keir Starmer.
Starmer announced his decision to step down as an MP in September after being ousted from No 10 by Andy Burnham.
Camden council has said the result is expected to be called between 2:30-4am UK time.
We’ll bring you the latest developments as we get them.

blocks.caption: Ballots being counted after polls closed in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection in London on Thursday.  Photograph: Carl Court/Getty Images

items: 18m agoCounting under way in Holborn and St Pancras byelection

blocks.text: Zack Polanski’s had a tricky week leading up to the byelection amid criticism he showed a lack of leadership over a policy equating Zionism with racism adopted at last weekend’s Green party conference
Polanski missed the vote on it in Brighton in order to campaign in the Holborn and St Pancras byelection.

But the Greens’ adoption of the policy has been highly contentious – drawing sharp rebukes from mainstream UK parties, British Jewish groups and Israel – while also prompting four of five Green MPs to publicly reject the move.

The motion said Zionism – the movement for a Jewish state – should be “treated as any other form of racism” and called for Israel to be replaced by a single Palestinian state. The head of the Jewish Greens condemned it and said she might leave the party, although it was supported by some Jewish Greens.

Even members who supported large parts of the motion were unhappy about its narrow conception of Zionism which some fear could brand those in favour of the idea of a Jewish homeland – but not specifically the modern-day state of Israel – as racist.
The English and Welsh Greens are facing international ostracism after their adoption of the policy drew dismay from the group representing European Greens.

blocks.text: Peter Walker
Holborn and St Pancras is, under normal circumstances, a Labour stronghold.

Keir Starmer won it with a majority of 11,500 at the 2024 general election despite strong challenges from the Greens and a leftwing independent candidate, who is not standing again and has endorsed Zack Polanski. In 2019 Starmer won by nearly 28,000 votes.

Polanski has run a highly energetic campaign. He has mobilised a large numbers of supporters to knock on doors, mimicking February’s Gorton and Denton byelection, where the Greens overcame an even bigger Labour majority to take the seat.

blocks.caption: Green leader Zack Polanski (second right) campaigning on the streets of Holborn and St Pancras last month. Photograph: Andy Hall/The Guardian

blocks.text: However, the political landscape has changed. Shortly after Gorton and Denton, YouGov polling put the Greens briefly above Labour, on a peak of 21%. The most recent equivalent had Polanksi’s party on 11%, 16 points behind Labour.

Burnham, who succeeded Starmer as prime minister in July, is seen as having revitalised Labour, and used his speech at the party’s annual conference last month to set out a more ambitious and left-leaning collection of policies.

Polanski’s fortunes, in contrast, appear to have declined, especially since last weekend’s Green party conference where a vote by members to adopt a policy equating Zionism with racism and calling for Israel to be replaced by a single Palestinian state prompted condemnation and splits in the party.
